top_choice_rationale: Ionizable lipid nanoparticles are chemistry in the strict sense: pH-dependent charge, lipid phase behaviour and nonbilayer structure govern assembly and endosomal release of lipid-nucleic acid particles. The achievement is mature (siRNA therapy since 2018, mRNA vaccines at global scale) and the carrier was not covered by the 2023 Medicine prize. Attribution to the Vancouver trio is the open weakness, so I rank the cleanly attributed Buchwald-Hartwig pair (P001) second and the protein degradation proposals next, since no degrader is yet approved.
recusal_note: Own research is lipid self-assembly and membrane biophysics, directly adjacent to the P005 subject; no specific personal tie to the proposed laureates is apparent from the profile. Lund colleagues Heiner Linke and Peter Somfai sit on the committee, and Linke proposes P004.
